title: AI underwriting: can it help underwriters, and who is using it?
description: Where AI pays in underwriting: the reading, not the decision. 19 tools checked, the US and EU rules, our benchmark data and three builds.
summary: AI underwriting goes beyond scanning: it pulls facts from applications, statements and broker emails, and drafts a risk score with reasons for the underwriter[^12][^21][^14]. Underwriters decide faster, and a named person still decides[^4][^2]. It fits small-business lenders, life insurers with a rules engine[^19], and commercial insurers swamped by broker submissions[^7].
humanRole: Underwriter: decides whether to offer, decline or price, after reviewing what the software recommends.[^34] In New York, an adverse decision notice should name the information used and its source.[^37][^2]
Credit officer at a lender: owns each decline and its reasons.[^4] For a scoring model, those reasons must be the factors it actually scored.[^16]
Head of underwriting: sits on the AI committee with claims, compliance and legal.[^38][^31] Checking AI against expert review is one validation method the bulletin names.[^38]

Model reviewer at a bank lender: an expert independent of the builder challenges a scoring model before first use.[^40] Bank regulators' 2026 guidance calls this "effective challenge" and leaves generative AI out of scope.[^40][^39]
teamAfter: Referred and complex files become the core job.[^18] BLS already lists reviewing software recommendations among underwriters' duties.[^34]
Underwriters get back admin hours: 39% to 43% of their time goes to admin today.[^1][^7]
Flagged gaps go back to people: underwriters contact field representatives, medical staff and others for what the file lacks.[^34][^12]
Testing for unfair outcomes, before use and on a schedule after, becomes standing work.[^2][^15] Among US firms using AI, 66% use it only to help staff; 2% saw AI-related employment fall.[^36]
verdict: Property and casualty (P&C) underwriters spend about 4 in 10 hours on admin AI can take on[^1][^7].
Start AI on the reading: statements, tax returns, broker submissions and referred-case evidence[^21][^18].
AI now reads financial documents well; scans still trip it, so check each fact.[^12][^42]
A named underwriter keeps the decision, with reasons a regulator can check[^4][^2].
Test on 50 past files before you buy; vendor speed figures are their customers' claims[^20][^27].

pickElse: Consumer lending where the score is the product: start with the AI credit scoring guide[^29]. The decline reasons are the regulated part[^4][^16].

Life and health insurer: start from a rules engine such as Swiss Re MagnumXP or Munich Re ALLFINANZ[^17][^19]. AI earns its keep summarising the evidence on referred cases so the underwriter decides faster, not making the call[^18][^19].

ownData.title: Which underwriting steps can AI take on today?
ownData.intro: AI can take on intake, fact extraction and a draft risk score today; picking among look-alike tables and the final decision still need a person[^12][^16]. Our read of each step comes from our own benchmark of AI reading long financial documents[^12] and the published studies below. That benchmark used public private-fund reports, not loan or insurance files[^12].
rows: Intake: read applications, broker emails, forms
Yes, with a second model checking

Yes, if every fact cites its page and quote
The top nine tools were within 2 facts of each other (FinExtractBench hard round)[^12]
Pick the right number among look-alike tables

7 of 10 tools took the wrong table on one 57-page report (FinExtractBench)[^12]
Chat models rated their wrong answers 70 to 100 (FinExtractBench)[^12]
Yes, if its stated reasons are the factors it scored[^16]; logistic regression stays the most transparent choice[^14]

A standard machine-learning model beat chat models at predicting loan defaults, and the same method tops a credit-scoring review[^13][^14]. MassMutual's machine-learned life score beat traditional underwriting on claims[^5][^30].
A person, using the model's reasons
Reg B (the US rule on credit decisions) requires specific reasons[^4][^16]. New York's insurance regulator (NYDFS) expects them in Circular Letter 7[^2].
ownData.note: Your documents will differ, which is why the first step of any build is a benchmark on your own files.

example.input: A small-business loan application, 12 months of bank statements and two years of tax returns.
example.output: Average monthly revenue, existing debt payments and two flagged risks, each with its page and quote. Plus a draft risk score with its main reasons, for the underwriter to accept or change.

recipes.name: 1. Commercial insurance: submission intake
recipes.when: Commercial insurers and MGAs (managing general agents, which underwrite for a carrier) whose underwriters key in broker submissions. Admin takes 41% to 43% of their time.[^7]
flow: Broker email, forms and loss runs (claims history) land in a queue the ops lead owns
AI extracts each fact with page and quote
AI checks appetite (the risks you want to write) and clearance (has another broker already sent this risk?); an underwriting assistant resolves flagged facts
Underwriter works the queue best fit first and decides
recipes.cost: Reading: about 12 to 15 cents a long fund report in our test[^12]. Intake products publish no price[^23]; a Zavient build is quoted per job, not listed here.

recipes.name: 2. Small-business lending: file to decision
recipes.when: Lenders whose underwriters spend the day reading statements and returns.
flow: Bank statements and tax returns land in a queue the ops lead owns
AI spreads statements and returns into your template, meaning it copies each figure into your standard credit-analysis layout
An underwriting assistant clears flagged facts
Explainable model drafts a score with its reasons
recipes.cost: Reading: under 1 cent to about 30 cents a long fund report in our test[^12]. The build, including a scorecard you own, is quoted per job, not listed here.

recipes.name: 3. Life insurance: evidence summary for the rules engine
recipes.when: Life and health carriers with an existing rules engine.

Clean cases: offer drafted, an underwriter spot-checks a sample
Others: referred to an underwriter, who decides
recipes.cost: Rules engines such as MagnumXP and ALLFINANZ publish no price; you contact the vendor[^17][^19]. The AI reading layer is quoted per job, and you can benchmark and swap it.

rules.name: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9
rules.what: US lenders must give notice of a decline within 30 days, with the specific main reasons or the right to get them[^4]. For a scoring model, the reasons must be the factors it actually scored[^16].

rules.name: NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7
rules.what: New York insurers should test AI and outside data for unfair discrimination and keep board oversight[^2]. They stay responsible for vendor tools and should give specific reasons and data sources for adverse decisions[^2].

rules.name: NAIC Model Bulletin on AI
rules.what: The NAIC (the US state insurance regulators' body) asks insurers to keep a written AI program with governance, risk controls, testing and vendor oversight[^31]. 30 US jurisdictions have adopted it[^9]. California, Colorado and New York have their own rules instead[^9].

rules.name: Colorado SB21-169
rules.status: Life; auto and health from 15 Oct 2025
rules.what: Insurers must test outside data and models for unfair discrimination, fix harm found and show the Division how they test[^3][^15].

rules.name: EU AI Act, Annex III
rules.what: Credit scoring of people and life and health insurance risk pricing are high-risk uses[^6]. Those rules apply from 2 December 2027[^10][^11]. High-risk systems need automatic logs and human oversight, so plan both now if you operate in the EU[^32][^33].

howToTest: Before any AI, time 50 files from one line or one branch as your team handles them today. Record hours per file, decision turnaround and how many in-appetite files are left without a quote or decision.
Then take 50 past files with known outcomes, including your messiest scans and longest packets.
Have your underwriters write the right value for every fact before any AI reads the files, and lock that answer key.
Run each tool on the same files. Count wrong facts apart from blanks, and require a page and quote for every fact.
For scoring, compare an explainable model with your current method on the same past files. Check that the decline reasons make sense to an underwriter.
Measure cost and time per file, and how many files still need a person. Report files decided per underwriter per week, decision turnaround and in-appetite submissions left unquoted, before and after.
Multiply hours saved per file by files per week and your loaded hourly cost. That gives the weekly dollar value of the change.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy when your line is standard, the vendor already handles your submission formats, and you are happy to run inside its workbench.[^22] Most firms buy: 76% of enterprise AI uses are bought, not built.[^43]
buyVsBuild.build: Build when your own loss history and appetite are your edge, or when you need the reading step to feed systems you already own. The reading layer is swappable: in our benchmark the top nine models were within 2 facts of each other[^12]. The decision logic is yours.

watchOuts: You stay responsible for a vendor's model. New York and the NAIC bulletin both expect audit rights in vendor contracts where available[^2][^31].
Models can carry past bias into new decisions. New York and Colorado expect insurers to test for unfair outcomes across groups before use and on a schedule after[^2][^15].
A model's confidence score is not a warning sign. In our benchmark, wrong answers came back rated 70 to 100[^12].
Vendor claims such as faster quotes are the vendor's own figures[^23], often from chosen customers[^20][^27]. Ask for a benchmark on your own files.
Flagged facts need an owner: in our benchmark, look-alike tables tripped 7 of 10 tools on one report[^12]. Count flags per file, multiply by weekly files and name who clears them.

faq.a: AI underwriting is software that reads the file and pulls out each fact with its page and quote.[^12][^21] It can draft a risk score with its reasons for the underwriter to review.[^34] The underwriter still decides.[^34][^2]

faq.q: Can AI approve or decline an application on its own?
faq.a: Only for simple consumer loans, where BLS says underwriting may be fully automated.[^35] Either way, the lender still owes specific reasons for a decline.[^4] Insurers must hold vendor AI to the legal standards they meet themselves.[^38]

Not most of them: BLS projects insurance underwriter jobs to fall 4% from 2025 to 2035, citing automated underwriting software.[^34] It still expects about 6,800 openings a year.[^34] Among US firms using AI, 66% use it only to help staff; 2% saw AI-related employment fall.[^36]

faq.q: Do you have to explain a loan decline made with AI?
faq.a: Yes: Reg B requires specific reasons, and for a scoring model they must be the factors it scored.[^4][^16] The CFPB withdrew its 2022 circular on AI declines in May 2025, but the rule itself still applies.[^41][^4]

faq.q: How accurate is AI at reading underwriting files?
faq.a: AI is very accurate at reading clean documents: the best model in a Fraunhofer study got 96.5% of invoice fields right.[^42] Scans are harder: 87.5% on scanned receipts.[^42] In our own test, two models made zero mistakes on 30 long fund reports.[^12]

faq.q: What does AI underwriting software cost?
faq.a: AI underwriting is sold by quote, with no list price among 19 products we checked; reading a report cost under 1 cent to 30 cents.[^23][^29][^12] The reading cost is from our test on long fund reports.[^12] Budget from a quote scoped to one line of business, after a test on 50 of your files.[^20]

The decline-reasons answer now says the circular was withdrawn in May 2025 and that Reg B itself still applies; the model-reviewer role notes the 2026 bank guidance leaves generative AI out of scope.

answers.example: Yes, up to the decision: AI can pull revenue, debts and risks from statements and tax returns, each with its page and quote, and draft a score with reasons[^12][^14]. The underwriter accepts or changes it and makes the call[^4][^16].
answers.recipes: AI fits the reading steps: commercial submission intake, copying small-business statements and returns into your credit template, and summarising life-insurance medical evidence for your rules engine[^7][^12][^18]. The underwriter still decides in each one[^4][^2].
answers.table-1: Commercial insurers use intake and risk tools such as Sixfold, Cytora, Convr and Kalepa; life insurers use rules engines such as Swiss Re MagnumXP and Munich Re ALLFINANZ[^20][^22][^23][^27][^17][^19]. Named Sixfold users include Zurich North America, Guardian and Generali[^20].
answers.rules: Examiners and regulators will ask for specific decline reasons that match the factors scored, tests for unfair discrimination, vendor oversight and a written AI program with governance[^4][^16][^2][^3][^31]. In the EU, they will also ask for logs and human oversight from 2 Dec 2027[^32][^33][^10].
answers.benchmark: Lock an underwriter-written answer key on 50 past files, run each tool on the same files, and count wrong facts, cost and time per file[^12]. Time the same files done by hand first, so you have a before number.
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI underwriting goes wrong when models carry past bias, report high confidence on wrong answers, take the wrong look-alike table, or arrive with vendor speed claims you never tested[^2][^15][^12][^23]. You also stay responsible for any vendor's model[^2][^31].
answers.something-else: Start somewhere else for consumer lending where the score is the product, life and health underwriting, or pricing questions[^29][^17][^24]. Those point to the AI credit scoring guide, a rules engine such as Swiss Re MagnumXP, or a pricing platform such as Akur8[^29][^17][^24].
answers.human-role: Your team keeps every underwriting decision: the underwriter offers, declines or prices, the credit officer owns each decline's reasons, and an independent reviewer challenges the model first[^34][^4][^40]. The head of underwriting sits on the AI committee[^38].
answers.team-after: After AI does the reading, your team works the referred and complex files, chases what the file lacks, and tests for unfair outcomes on a schedule[^18][^34][^2][^15]. Underwriters also get back admin time, now 39% to 43% of their week[^1][^7].
answers.buy-or-build: Buy when your line is standard and the vendor already reads your submission formats[^22]; build when your own loss history is your edge, because the reading layer is swappable[^12].
